name: Oakley Roman
life: “I still remember cutting a whole line of tiny names no camera would ever catch.” On Tuesday, near the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, Oakley checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I cut the lettering and found no mention of the founder or the chief. An ordinary wall has never required so much careful spelling.
appearance: Oakley has thick, tightly coiled hair, fine brows over wide-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. It usually goes with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. When somebody else has the floor, Oakley turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Oakley is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Oakley is concerned.
agenda: To spell every ordinary name correctly on the wall.
family: Victor Lowe is Oakley’s cousin raised in the same household. Oakley can stop the walk at any corner. Victor chooses the familiar route. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *The first language*, Victor says, “I buy books in our first language and never open them myself.”
connections: Zoe Nash. The sign painter asks how the brother who listens would want his name spelled.
